name: Simvastatin
summary: A lipophilic statin with potent LDL lowering that depends heavily on CYP3A4, making drug interactions a central clinical consideration.
mechanism: Prodrug lactone converted to the active hydroxy acid, which competitively inhibits HMG-CoA reductase and upregulates hepatic LDL receptors.

dosing.adult: 20–40 mg once daily in the evening (range 5–80 mg)
dosing.maxDose: 40 mg/day (80 mg no longer recommended due to myopathy risk)
dosing.renalAdjustment: Start at 5 mg/day in severe renal impairment

safety.pregnancy: Contraindicated in pregnancy (US FDA category X)
contraindications: Concurrent strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., itraconazole, ketoconazole, clarithromycin, HIV protease inhibitors)
warnings: Myopathy/rhabdomyolysis, particularly with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or high doses

indications: Primary and secondary prevention of atherosclerotic cardiovascular events
clinicalPearls: Evening dosing aligns with peak hepatic cholesterol synthesis.
Avoid grapefruit juice and screen for CYP3A4 inhibitor co-prescriptions.
good: Patients needing substantial LDL reduction at low cost.
bad: Patients on strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or with prior statin intolerance.
